schema_note: This format is internal to pcaptriage and may change in any release. It is not a stability contract; do not build tooling that depends on its shape.

tool.name: pcaptriage
tool.build: Partial build: 2 of the 15 v1 rules are implemented (R01 zero-window-stall, R04 server-response-outlier). Every other condition in the v1 rule set was not looked for at all.

checks.name: zero-window-stall
checks.summary: A receiver advertised a zero window having previously advertised non-zero, blocking the sender until a window update arrived.

checks.name: server-response-outlier
checks.summary: A server:port took materially longer to begin responding than its peers in the same capture, with network round-trip time subtracted.

findings.title: One server much slower to respond than its peers — 10.4.4.1:443
findings.observation: Responded in 2.6s at p95 (max 2.6s) while the other 8 servers in this capture are under 40ms at p95. Measured from last request byte to first response byte, with network round-trip time subtracted — so this is time spent on the server, not on the network.
findings.check_next: application or backend dependency latency on 10.4.4.1. The network path to this host looks comparable to its peers.

findings.title: One server much slower to respond than its peers — 10.4.4.2:443
findings.observation: Responded in 1.5s at p95 (max 1.5s) while the other 8 servers in this capture are under 40ms at p95. Measured from last request byte to first response byte, with network round-trip time subtracted — so this is time spent on the server, not on the network.
findings.check_next: application or backend dependency latency on 10.4.4.2. The network path to this host looks comparable to its peers.

findings.title: Receiver stopped accepting data — 10.2.2.7:5432
findings.observation: Advertised a zero receive window 4 times, stalling the sender for 4.2s total (longest single stall 2.9s).
findings.check_next: the receiving application on 10.2.2.7 — a zero window means the application is not reading from its socket buffer fast enough. Look at CPU, blocked threads, or a downstream dependency on that host.

findings.observation: Advertised a zero receive window 2 times, stalling the sender for 600ms total (longest single stall 600ms).
findings.check_next: the receiving application on 10.2.2.9 — a zero window means the application is not reading from its socket buffer fast enough. Look at CPU, blocked threads, or a downstream dependency on that host.

findings.check_next: the receiving application on 10.2.2.8 — a zero window means the application is not reading from its socket buffer fast enough. Look at CPU, blocked threads, or a downstream dependency on that host.

notes.text: Not assessed: whether the capture host dropped packets before writing them. The classic pcap format has no field to record it, so this file cannot say either way. Packets dropped by the capturing machine look the same as packets lost on the network. If that distinction matters here, re-capturing in pcapng format would record the count.
